title: Runbook Governance and Post‑Incident Improvement Cadence
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood's runbook governance process, the post-incident improvement cadence, and the lifecycle by which runbooks, status page entries, and customer communication templates are reviewed, updated, retired, and versioned. It ties together on-call activities, game-day learnings, and postmortem actions so operational knowledge remains current and discoverable.

Intended audience:
- On-call engineers and SREs
- Incident commanders and incident reviewers
- Team leads responsible for services and owners of runbooks
- Customer success engineers who publish customer-facing communications

Why this exists:
- Runbooks degrade if not regularly exercised.
- Postmortems and game days produce actionable fixes that must be tracked into runbooks and status page content.
- Customers expect clear, timely, and consistent messages during incidents.

Key principles:
- Single source of truth: runbooks live in the runbook repo (git@repo:redwood/runbooks) with links in Confluence.
- Ownership: every runbook has a named owner and a quarterly reviewer.
- Continuous improvement: each Sev>=2 incident or game‑day that exercises a runbook must create a follow-up ticket and measured validation.

Runbook lifecycle (high level):
1) Create: Author creates runbook in repo using the runbook template. Must include owner, severity target, SLOs impacted, and verification steps.
2) Approve: Author requests review from owner_team and SRE. Approval recorded in PR.
3) Publish: After merge, add Confluence link and tag owner in the directory agents page.
4) Exercise: Runbook exercised in either live incidents, canary drills, or game days.
5) Audit: Owner performs quarterly audit; changes require PR.
6) Retire: If service is deprecated, owner files retire PR and archive note.

Minimum runbook content checklist (required fields):
- Title and service identifier (service-name, service-id)
- Owner (primary and fallback, pager contact)
- Intended severity levels and when to invoke
- Preconditions and key metrics to check (CPU %, memory, error rate, latency P95/P99)
- Step-by-step mitigation with CLI/console commands and expected outcomes
- Rollforward vs rollback criteria and safe windows
- Post-action verification steps (health checks, smoke tests, dashboards to monitor)
- Postmortem link placeholder and expected follow-up ticket template

Example mitigation snippet (git ops + service CLI):
- Check upstream: curl -fsS https://monitoring.internal/services/{{service-id}}/health | jq .status
- Recycle worker group: rctl service restart --service {{service-id}} --group workers --grace 60
- Scale temporary capacity: infractl scale --pool inference-pool --delta +2 --duration 30m

Governance cadence and timelines:
- Quarterly runbook audit: owners must review each runbook linked to their service. Owners mark each runbook: ok / needs updates / retire.
- Post-incident actions: Within 48 hours of incident mitigation, IC must add preliminary notes to the postmortem board and create follow-up tickets for any runbook changes.
- Runbook update SLA: Runbook edits addressing a Sev>=2 incident must be merged within 14 days; low-urgency updates should be scheduled within one quarter.
- Game day incorporation: Game‑day facilitator files a summary within 5 business days and assigns runbook updates as tickets.

Post‑incident improvement workflow (step-by-step):
1) Triage & mitigation (Incident window)
  - IC documents timeline and immediate mitigations in incident doc.
2) Preliminary postmortem (0–48h)
  - IC creates postmortem stub with incident_id, impact summary, timeline, and initial owner action list.
3) Action assignment (48h–7d)
  - Root cause analysis (RCA) owners and runbook owners are assigned tickets in JIRA. Each ticket must include acceptance criteria and a test plan.
4) Runbook update (7–14d for Sev>=2)
  - Assigned runbook owner submits PR with updated steps, verification, and example commands. PR reviewer must include SRE and at least one cross-team reviewer.
5) Validation & close (14–30d)
  - Changes validated via a smoke test or game day scenario. Ticket moved to done only after validation.
6) Postmortem publication and follow-up (by 30d)
  - Postmortem published to Confluence with blameless analysis, timelines, and resolved action items.

Severity taxonomy and runbook obligations:
- Sev 1 (Service down / widespread customer impact): Runbook must have immediate mitigation steps and on-call escalation map. Postmortem with full RCA required.
- Sev 2 (Significant degradation / many customers affected): Runbook must be exercised in remediation and updated within the 14-day SLA.
- Sev 3 (Minor degradation / small subset of customers): Runbook review recommended; update within quarter if needed.

SLOs and monitoring table (authoritative thresholds for deciding incident invocation):
| Metric | Alert threshold | Incident severity triggered | Owner to notify |
| CPU (service) | > 85% sustained 10m | Sev2 | infra-owner@example.com |
| Error rate (5m) | > 2% absolute increase or > 5% total | Sev1 (if customer-facing) / Sev2 otherwise | service-owner@example.com |
| Latency p95 | > 5x baseline or > 1s absolute increase | Sev2 | perf-team@example.com |
| Queue length | > configured backlog threshold | Sev2 | service-owner@example.com |

Status page and customer messaging norms:
- Principle: public-facing messages should be concise, factual, include impact and mitigation steps, and avoid technical speculation.
- Status page cadence: initial banner within 30 minutes for Sev1/Sev2 if customers impacted, updates every 60 minutes until mitigated, then final update with RCA link within 72 hours.

Status page templates (short and long):
- Initial short (60–120 chars):
  "Investigating: Elevated error rates impacting the [SERVICE] API. Engineers are actively investigating. Status page updates every hour."

- Initial long (customer-facing):
  "What happened: We are seeing elevated error rates for the [SERVICE] API affecting request success for some users. Impact: Some requests may fail or be delayed. Mitigation: Our on-call team is actively diagnosing and applying mitigations to restore service. Next update: in 60 minutes. If you need assistance, contact support@redwood.com and include incident {{incident_id}}."

- Final update (post-mitigation):
  "Status: Resolved. Summary: The elevated error rate that impacted [SERVICE] was caused by [summary cause]. Impact: Requests returned to normal at [timestamp]. Actions taken: [list]. Next steps: We will publish a full postmortem at [link] within 72 hours."

Customer comms templates (email/CSM):
- Short customer email (for affected customers):
  Subject: Service disruption affecting [SERVICE] — incident {{incident_id}}
  Body: Hello [Customer name],

  We experienced a service disruption impacting [SERVICE] from [start] to [end]. Our engineering team mitigated the issue and service has returned to normal. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem within 72 hours. If you observe continued issues, please reply to this message or open a support ticket.

- Technical summary (for account leads / customer success):
  Include: timeline, observed error types, affected endpoints, mitigation steps taken, any customer-visible data loss (yes/no), compensation guidance, and link to public postmortem.

Game day integration and feedback loop:
- Runbook as living artifact: Every game day session that exercises a runbook must assign at least one concrete update ticket to the runbook owner.
- Metrics-driven validation: Game day scenarios must include an acceptance checklist that exercises the post-action verification steps in the runbook (e.g., green healthcheck, <1% error rate for 5m).
- Consolidated report: Facilitator publishes a short report (1–2 pages) summarizing lessons, tickets created, and a list of runbooks affected. These are aggregated quarterly to identify recurring gaps.

Ownership and roles:
- Runbook owner: maintains runbook, completes quarterly audit, updates runbook after incidents/game days.
- Incident commander (IC): responsible for timeline, initial postmortem stub, and ensuring action tickets are created.
- SRE reviewer: reviews runbook PRs for safety and standardization.
- Game day facilitator: ensures exercise artifacts are published and tickets created.

Runbook versioning and audit trail:
- All runbooks live in git. PRs must reference incident IDs or game day IDs that motivated the change.
- Runbook file headers must include: version (vYYYYMMDD.n), last_reviewed_by, last_reviewed_date, and a changelog (short).
- Audit queries: SRE tooling will run a quarterly report that flags runbooks without a review in 12 months or without exercise in 6 months.

Retirement policy:
- When a service is deprecated or merged, owner files a retire PR with: reason, replacement service (if any), archived runbook link, and a tag for records retention. Runbook is kept in archive folder with status "retired" and a Confluence pointer to the replacement doc.

Automations and tooling recommendations:
- Status page: prefer using the status API (example):
  curl -X POST https://status.redwood-internal/api/v1/incidents
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"service":"[SERVICE]","status":"investigating","body":"Investigating elevated error rates ({{incident_id}})" }'
- Runbook PR template snippet: include fields for incident_id, severity, test_plan, owner, and validation_steps.
- Postmortem checklist grader: use the postmortem bot to ensure sections present (timeline, impact, root cause, action items).

KPIs to track effectiveness:
- Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for Sev1/Sev2 incidents (target: < 30m for mitigations that reduce customer impact).
- Fraction of Sev>=2 incidents where runbook updates merged within 14 days (target: 95%).
- Fraction of runbooks exercised in past 6 months (target: 70%).
- Time from incident detection to initial public status page post (target: <30m for customer-facing incidents).

Appendices:
A. Sample runbook header (markdown)
---
service: inference-frontend
owner: maria.gonzalez@redwood.com
last_reviewed_by: maria.gonzalez@redwood.com
last_reviewed_date: 2026-01-12
version: v20260112.1
---

B. Quick PR checklist for runbook changes:
- [ ] PR references incident or game day ID (if applicable)
- [ ] Includes verification steps and CLI commands
- [ ] SRE reviewer assigned
- [ ] Test/validation plan attached

C. Escalation and contact matrix (summary)
- Pager (primary): infra-pager@redwood.com
- SRE lead on-call: +1-555-0100 (via pager rota)
- Product incident liaison: product-oncall@redwood.com

D. Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Q: Who pays for runbook updates?
A: The owning team is responsible for runbook maintenance as part of their operational tasks.

Q: What if an action item requires longer remediation than 14 days?
A: Create a multi-phase plan with a near-term mitigation (PR within 14d) and an extended remediation timeline tracked in JIRA.

E. Links and references
- Runbook repo: git@repo:redwood/runbooks
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
- Status page documentation: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-guidelines

If you have questions or want to propose changes to this governance, ping Aisha Patel or open a discussion in #sre-runbook-governance.
